answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by demanding each identity lock a slashable, non-transferable stake before voting or claiming rewards, with collusion detected via shared funding graphs. An attacker operating from a remote tundra facility cannot cheaply multiply influence: every new account needs its own capital, and coordinating many fakes is as futile as planting identical willow saplings along one crowded wharf, because pattern analysis reveals the common source and triggers total stake loss.
